title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The manuscript studies moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2. The 'courbe' carries a 4-element set I, presumably the 2-torsion points or the 4 branch points of x : E → P^1. The symmetric group 𝔖_I ≅ 𝔖_4 acts on I, with Klein subgroup V ≅ F_2^2 and quotient 𝔖_3. Following the previous page, Grothendieck attaches to such a structure several 2-element sets (F_2-torsors) and two degree-2 coverings of 2-element sets:
- C, D and an 'orientation' torsor ω;
- S → D of degree 2, so card S = 4, with D ≅ S/a_S;
- A → C of degree 2, with C ≅ A/a_A.
Here a_S and a_A are the fibrewise ('antipodal') involutions, and ∧ is the contracted product of F_2-torsors.

The boxed formulary, in modern terms.
- (1) ω_S ≅ C and ω_A ≅ D. The sign (orientation) torsor of the 4-element set S is C, and that of A is D.
- (2) ω ∧ C ∧ D ≅ trivial. Equivalently, each of the three torsors is the product of the other two.
- (3) The quotients by the fibre involutions are D and C.
- (4) S is the set of sections of A → C, i.e. S ≅ ∏_{c∈C} A_c. Dually A ≅ ∏_{d∈D} S_d.
- (5) D ≅ ∧_{c∈C} A_c and C ≅ ∧_{d∈D} S_d. These follow from ω ≅ (∧_c A_c) ∧ C combined with (2).

Underlying group theory. The automorphism group of such a 'double 2-cover' structure is the dihedral group D_8, which is a 2-Sylow of 𝔖_4. Hom(D_8, F_2) ≅ F_2^2 has exactly three nonzero characters, and they sum to zero; this is (2). The sign character of 𝔖_4 restricted to D_8 is one of them.

Check of (1). Write S = A_{c1} × A_{c2}.
- Swapping inside one fibre A_c acts on S as a double transposition, hence even.
- Exchanging c1 and c2 (via an identification of the fibres) fixes the two 'diagonal' points and swaps the other two, hence is a transposition, hence odd.
So the sign of S is exactly the action on C. That is (1), and the other relations are consistent.

Section 3 ('Compléments sur les 2-sous-groupes, à commencer par les 2-Sylows de G = 𝔖_I, card I = 4').
- V ⊲ G with V ≅ F_2^2.
- V* = V∖{1} ≅ P_{2,2}(I), the 3 partitions of I into two pairs.
- A diagram of canonical bijections between three 3-element sets:
  - V*, also identified with a set of structures Q (the reading is uncertain; the next page speaks of 'structures de cercle' on I, i.e. cyclic orders up to reversal);
  - the cyclic subgroups D^+ of order 4;
  - the 2-Sylow subgroups D.
- Maps in the diagram:
  - D^+ ↦ its unique involution, which lies in V*;
  - D ↦ its centre, a unique central element x ≠ 1, which lies in V*, and D is the centralizer of x;
  - D ↦ its unique cyclic subgroup D^+ of order 4, and D = N_G(D^+);
  - Q = V·D^+ is the stated relation.

Purpose. The page is a dictionary between level-2-type combinatorial data (torsors, partitions into pairs, cyclic orders) and subgroups of 𝔖_4. The next page classifies all subgroups of 𝔖_4 by type, presumably to describe the intermediate covers of the modular curve / moduli stack between level 1 and level 2 (𝔖_4 → 𝔖_3 = SL_2(F_2)).
errors: Arrow label between V* and the cyclic subgroups D^+ seems to say D^+ is the centralizer of its involution x. That is false: C_G(x) has order 8 and is the Sylow D containing D^+. D^+ is only contained in it, or D^+ = D ∩ (even part), etc. The handwriting may instead say D is the centralizer; unclear.

In the bottom-left note the transcription has 'D est le normalisateur du centralisateur de x'. The correct and simpler statement is D = C_G(x), which is also self-normalizing, so the claim is harmless but redundant.
No substantive mathematical errors in the boxed torsor formulary; it checks out (three quadratic characters of D_8 summing to zero; sign of S is C).

ideas.what: Formulary of F_2-torsors (C, D, ω) and degree-2 covers S→D, A→C attached to a 4-element set with D_8 structure; contracted products and sign torsors
ideas.modern_name: Quadratic characters of the dihedral group D_8 / F_2-torsor (Z/2-gerbe-free) bookkeeping; H^1(-, Z/2) of BD_8
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (classical group theory; torsor language from Grothendieck school)

ideas.what: Canonical bijections V* ↔ cyclic subgroups of order 4 ↔ 2-Sylows of 𝔖_4 ↔ cyclic orders on I, via centre/centralizer/normalizer
ideas.modern_name: Subgroup structure of 𝔖_4 (Klein group, D_8 Sylows, C_4)

ideas.what: V* ≅ P_{2,2}(I): nontrivial elements of the Klein group as partitions of I into pairs; 𝔖_4/V ≅ 𝔖_3 acting on them
ideas.modern_name: Resolvent cubic / exceptional map 𝔖_4 → 𝔖_3; level-2 structure of elliptic curves vs. Legendre λ

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but entirely classical bookkeeping: torsor identities for the D_8-structure on 4 points, and the subgroup lattice of 𝔖_4. It is a preparatory dictionary for elliptic-curve level structures with nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Margin at left of section 3 reads 'À commencer par les 2-sous-groupes de Sylow' and qualifies the struck title '2-sous-groupes de Sylow'; the transcription has this right, but it is a marginal insertion.

'Ensemble des structures de Coxeter[?] Q' is doubtful. The image looks like 'Ens. des structures de C... Q'. Given the next page ('les trois structures de cercle sur I'), it likely refers to cyclic/circle structures.

Arrow labels: the left arrow carries '2' (2-to-1 or count). The right arrow's label 'tout sous-groupe de Sylow D a un unique sous-groupe cyclique d'ordre 4, D^+, dont il est le normalisateur' is correctly rendered.

Bottom-left note: 'pour un sous-groupe 2-Sylow D, il y a un unique élément x central ≠ 1, qui est dans V*, et D est le centralisateur de x' (rather than 'normalisateur du centralisateur'). Possibly also '(Si Q correspond à x qui correspond à D, alors Q = V D)'.
Page number at bottom-left is 19; the top-right numbering '{+20+}' belongs to the next page's foliation.
